University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Превращаем температурное разнообразие в сигнал для обучения языковых моделей
ru.desc: В этой работе предлагается новый метод Temperature-Grouped Reinforcement Learning (TGRL) для эффективного обучения больших языковых моделей с проверяемыми вознаграждениями. Ключевая идея заключается в том, чтобы превратить разнообразие, создаваемое разными температурами при генерации текста, в явный сигнал для обучения модели. Метод разделяет выборки на подмножества с низкой и высокой температурой, оценивает прибыль от исследования через контраст вознаграждений, и использует дивергенцию Йенсена-Шеннона для распределения этого сигнала на уровне отдельных токенов. Эксперименты показывают, что TGRL достигает той же точности на 36% быстрее, чем существующие методы, и значительно улучшает результаты на математических задачах, задачах программирования и взаимодействии с веб-сайтами.

en.title: Boosting Exploration Efficiency with TGRL
en.desc: This paper introduces Temperature-Grouped Reinforcement Learning (TGRL), a novel approach to enhance exploration in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. TGRL utilizes temperature-induced diversity as a training signal by dividing rollout groups into low- and high-temperature subsets, allowing for better estimation of exploration gains. By applying Jensen-Shannon divergence, TGRL effectively allocates exploration rewards at the token level, leading to faster convergence without increasing the sample budget. The results demonstrate that TGRL outperforms existing methods across multiple benchmarks, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency.

zh.title: 温度分组强化学习：提升探索效率的创新方法
zh.desc: 在强化学习中，探索效率常常是一个主要瓶颈。本文提出了一种新的方法，称为温度分组强化学习（TGRL），它将温度引起的多样性转化为明确的训练信号。TGRL通过对低温和高温子集的奖励对比来估计探索收益，并利用Jensen-Shannon散度将这一信号分配到每个token上。实验结果表明，TGRL在多个基准测试中显著优于传统方法，且在不增加样本预算的情况下，训练速度提高了36%。

papers.title: What Makes Recurrence Effective in Looped Language Models?
papers.abstract: Abstract  Looped language models (LoopLMs) increase computational depth through parameter sharing, offering a path to scale inference computation without adding parameters. However, it remains unclear when additional recurrence is beneficial and how architectural choices affect its effectiveness. Through controlled experiments, we systematically examine (1) when recurrence helps, (2) where it should be applied, and (3) how its conditioning affects performance. Our evaluation covers inference budgets below, within, and beyond the training horizon under knowledge and reasoning tasks. (1) We find that recurrence can improve reasoning beyond the training horizon while degrading knowledge performance, but harder reasoning instances do not consistently benefit more. (2) Performance also depends on how distinct layers and recurrent iterations are allocated, showing that effective depth alone is insufficient to predict behavior. Non-recurrent output layers improve robustness to under-unrolling, while the preferred placement of input and output layers varies with inference budget. (3) Finally, we find that conventional initial-state injection offers limited robustness to varying recurrence depth. We therefore propose history-state injection as an alternative, and show that channel-wise history-state injection combined with timestep conditioning offers a low-cost and more effective design, better preserving knowledge under extended unrolling while improving robustness across inference budgets. Overall, our results clarify when recurrent computation helps, where it fails, and offer practical guidelines for designing LoopLMs across variable inference budgets.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Рекуррентные циклы без новых параметров: когда и как их использовать
ru.desc: В статье исследуются зациклические языковые модели (LoopLMs), которые увеличивают глубину вычислений через переиспользование параметров, позволяя масштабировать инференс без добавления новых весов. Авторы проводят систематический анализ того, когда рекуррентность полезна, где её применять и как её архитектурные решения влияют на производительность. Они обнаруживают, что рекуррентность помогает при решении сложных задач, но ухудшает производительность на задачах знаний, а размещение слоёв критически влияет на результаты. Как решение предлагается новый метод инициализации истории состояния с покоординатным кондиционированием, который лучше сохраняет знания при расширенной развёртке и улучшает устойчивость к различным бюджетам инференса.

en.title: Unlocking the Power of Recurrence in Looped Language Models
en.desc: This paper explores Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) that enhance computational depth by sharing parameters, allowing for efficient scaling of inference without increasing the number of parameters. The authors conduct experiments to determine when recurrence is beneficial, how to apply it effectively, and how it influences performance across different tasks. They discover that while recurrence can enhance reasoning capabilities beyond the training horizon, it may negatively impact knowledge performance, and the arrangement of layers significantly affects outcomes. The study introduces a new method called history-state injection, which improves robustness and knowledge retention during extended unrolling, providing practical design guidelines for LoopLMs in various inference scenarios.

zh.title: 循环语言模型的设计与优化
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了循环语言模型（LoopLMs）在推理计算中的应用，特别是参数共享如何增加计算深度而不增加参数数量。研究表明，循环结构在推理超出训练范围时可以改善推理能力，但在知识性能上可能会有所下降。通过系统实验，论文分析了循环的有效性与层次分配、输入输出层的放置以及初始状态注入的关系。最后，提出了历史状态注入作为一种替代方案，以提高在不同推理预算下的鲁棒性和知识保留能力。

papers.title: Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Abstract  Prompt injection against LLM agents becomes much stronger when the injected instruction is wrapped in the model's own chat template. A forged template marker such as <|im_start|> can reach the model either as a single reserved control token or as a sequence of ordinary subword tokens. The two decode to exactly the same text, and because tokenization runs on the server, the defender rather than the attacker decides which one the model receives. We use this to measure how much of the injected instruction's authority comes from the reserved token's learned representation. Encoding the forged markers as subwords, with the text held fixed and a control for the extra tokens this adds, lowers attack success on the InjecAgent benchmark by 39 to 66 percentage points on three of four open-weight families, and the gap carries over to multi-turn agent tasks in AgentDojo. On Qwen3-8B the gap is 8 points, because without reserved ids the model still recognises the forged turn from its text by reasoning; suppressing the reasoning block widens the gap to 50. The authority sits in the single learned vector at the marker position: the mean of the marker's subword vectors does not reproduce it, the vector of the nearest ordinary token restores the attack on Llama-3.1, and an adaptive attacker who searches for non-reserved markers finds such embedding neighbours on three of four families. In every base and instruction-tuned pair we test, instruction tuning strengthens the model's preference for reserved markers. The standard mitigation, a tokenizer option that encodes special tokens as ordinary subwords, applies only to tokens a configuration declares special, so in 33 of 67 distinct tokenizer configurations, covering 255 of the 400 most-downloaded chat models on Hugging Face, it leaves intact the tool-protocol tokens through which agents read untrusted tool output, and the gap persists on that channel.

ru.title: Власть зарезервированных токенов в инъекциях подсказок LLM
ru.desc: Исследование показывает, что инъекции подсказок в LLM-агентов становятся намного опаснее, когда вредоносная инструкция обёрнута в шаблон чата модели с использованием зарезервированных управляющих токенов. Авторы обнаружили, что власть атаки сосредоточена в специальных векторах представления этих токенов - когда форжированные маркеры кодируются обычными подсловами вместо зарезервированных токенов, эффективность атак снижается на 39-66 процентных пункта. Исследование демонстрирует, что стандартные защиты неполны: многие конфигурации токенизаторов оставляют уязвимыми токены протокола инструментов, через которые агенты читают недоверенные данные. Выводы раскрывают уязвимость архитектуры современных LLM и предлагают новые направления для разработки более надёжных защит.

en.title: Strengthening LLMs Against Prompt Injection Attacks
en.desc: This paper discusses how prompt injection attacks on large language model (LLM) agents can be more effective when the injected instructions mimic the model's own chat format. By using a forged template marker, attackers can manipulate the model's responses, but the authors show that encoding these markers as subwords significantly reduces the success of such attacks. The research reveals that the model's learned representation of reserved tokens plays a crucial role in the authority of the injected instructions. The findings suggest that standard mitigation strategies may not adequately protect against these vulnerabilities, especially in widely used chat models.

zh.title: 提升模型安全性的关键在于保留标记的使用
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了针对大型语言模型（LLM）代理的提示注入攻击，特别是当注入的指令被包装在模型自身的聊天模板中时，攻击的效果会更强。研究发现，伪造的模板标记如<|im_start|>可以作为单个保留控制标记或普通子词标记的序列到达模型。通过将伪造标记编码为子词，攻击成功率在多个开放权重模型上显著降低，尤其是在多轮代理任务中。结果表明，指令调优增强了模型对保留标记的偏好，且标准的缓解措施在许多情况下未能有效防止攻击。

papers.title: EpiCon: Collective Agent Learning through Co-Evolving Multimodal Memory
papers.abstract: Abstract  Agents can learn from past executions, but enabling different agents to reuse and build on one another's experience remains challenging. We introduce EpiCon, a shared multimodal memory framework for agent collective learning without updating host model parameters. EpiCon links question-level memory evolution to a persistent experience bank through two independently trained 2B models: a memory controller and a tree self-organizer. The controller jointly refines textual guidance and visual evidence across attempts and selectively includes visual memory. The self-organizer consolidates lessons hierarchically and retrieves experience and rules for new problems. We evaluate EpiCon on eleven benchmarks spanning four multimodal task domains, using two harnesses and multiple backbones. A frozen bank improves other systems even with a single solving attempt. A second harness raises the original system's macro-average score by 2.6 points across eleven benchmarks. Across four host configurations, EpiCon improves macro-average scores by 1.7 to 4.9 points over No Memory and reduces memory-operation time by 67\% to 74\% relative to backbone-sized memory models.

ru.title: Коллективная мудрость агентов через разделяемую мультимодальную память
ru.desc: В статье предлагается EpiCon — фреймворк для коллективного обучения агентов на основе разделяемой мультимодальной памяти без обновления параметров основной модели. Система использует два независимо обученных компактных модели: контроллер памяти, который уточняет текстовую информацию и визуальные доказательства, и древовидный самоорганизатор, который иерархически консолидирует накопленный опыт. Архитектура позволяет агентам переиспользовать опыт друг друга через постоянный банк опыта и автоматически извлекать релевантные примеры и правила для новых задач. Экспериментальная оценка на одиннадцати бенчмарках показывает, что EpiCon улучшает качество на 1.7-4.9 пункта и снижает вычислительные затраты на 67-74% по сравнению с моделями памяти размером с основную модель.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Shared Memory for Collective Learning
en.desc: EpiCon is a novel framework designed to enhance collective learning among agents by utilizing a shared multimodal memory system. It operates without altering the parameters of the host models, allowing agents to learn from a persistent experience bank. The framework consists of two key components: a memory controller that refines both textual and visual information, and a tree self-organizer that hierarchically consolidates knowledge for efficient retrieval. Evaluation results show that EpiCon significantly improves performance across various benchmarks while reducing memory operation time, demonstrating its effectiveness in agent collaboration and learning efficiency.

zh.title: EpiCon：智能体集体学习的新纪元
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为EpiCon的共享多模态记忆框架，旨在促进不同智能体之间的集体学习，而无需更新主模型参数。EpiCon通过两个独立训练的2B模型——记忆控制器和树形自组织者，将问题级记忆演变与持久经验库相连接。记忆控制器在多次尝试中共同优化文本指导和视觉证据，并选择性地包含视觉记忆，而自组织者则以层次方式整合经验教训，并为新问题检索经验和规则。通过在四个多模态任务领域的十一项基准测试中评估，EpiCon显著提高了系统的性能，并减少了记忆操作时间。

papers.title: WISE-ATTA: When to Ask for Labels in Budgeted Active Test-Time Adaptation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Active test-time adaptation (ATTA) improves robustness under distribution shift by updating a deployed model during inference while selectively querying supervision. However, most existing ATTA methods implicitly assume that supervision can be requested for every incoming test batch, which can incur substantial annotation cost over long test streams. In this work, we introduce budgeted ATTA in which labels are available for only a fraction of test batches. This formulation shifts the central challenge from deciding what to label within a batch to deciding when supervision should be applied over time. To address this challenge, we propose a budget-aware approach WISE-ATTA that allocates supervision over the test stream based on lightweight signals computed online, prioritizing periods where supervision is likely to be most useful. When a batch is selected for supervision, we further employ a drift-based sample selection criterion that targets samples exhibiting ongoing, unconverged adaptation dynamics, enabling effective updates from a single labeled example. We evaluate this approach on synthetic corruptions (ImageNet-C) and natural distribution shifts (ImageNet-R/K/A). Across settings, WISE-ATTA achieves competitive or improved performance compared to recent ATTA methods while requiring substantially fewer labels. Overall, we find that the timing of supervision is a key, yet underexplored, aspect of active test-time adaptation. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifaa/WISE-ATTA
affiliations: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security

ru.title: Расписание разметки важнее её объёма
ru.desc: В работе предлагается метод WISE-ATTA для активной адаптации модели во время инференса под распределение данных, когда доступна разметка только для небольшой доли батчей. Ключевая идея заключается в смещении фокуса с выбора объектов для разметки внутри батча на выбор оптимального времени запроса разметки на всём потоке тестовых данных. Метод использует лёгкие сигналы для определения периодов, когда дополнительная разметка принесёт наибольшую пользу, и критерий выбора образцов на основе дрифта для эффективного обновления модели. Экспериментально показано, что WISE-ATTA достигает конкурентных результатов на синтетических и естественных распределениях при значительно меньшем количестве требуемых меток.

en.title: Smart Supervision Timing for Efficient Model Adaptation
en.desc: This paper presents a new method called budgeted Active Test-Time Adaptation (ATTA) that enhances model robustness during inference when faced with changing data distributions. Unlike traditional ATTA methods that assume supervision can be requested for every test batch, this approach limits supervision to only a fraction of batches, reducing annotation costs. The proposed WISE-ATTA method intelligently decides when to apply supervision based on real-time signals, focusing on moments when it is most beneficial. Additionally, it uses a drift-based sample selection to effectively update the model with minimal labeled examples, demonstrating improved performance with fewer labels across various datasets.

zh.title: 优化监督时机，提升模型适应性
zh.desc: 主动测试时适应（ATTA）通过在推理过程中更新已部署的模型来提高对分布变化的鲁棒性，同时选择性地请求监督。然而，大多数现有的ATTA方法隐含地假设可以为每个测试批次请求监督，这在长时间的测试流中会产生大量的标注成本。本文提出了预算ATTA，其中标签仅对一部分测试批次可用，挑战转变为决定何时应用监督。我们提出了一种预算感知的方法WISE-ATTA，根据在线计算的轻量信号在测试流中分配监督，优先考虑监督最有用的时间段。

papers.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
papers.abstract: Abstract  Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), popularized by large language models, is a promising paradigm for scaling visual generative models. However, conventional token-wise MoE routes tokens independently within a homogeneous expert pool and regularizes expert usage toward uniformity, making it poorly matched to video data that is spatiotemporally redundant and semantically long-tailed. We show that existing visual MoEs fall into a uniformity trap: semantically under-organized routing, compounded by uniform expert-usage regularization, scatters coherent patches across disparate experts, causing routing fragmentation and structural distortion. To address this, we propose SplitMoE, a split-role sparse architecture that breaks the shackles of uniformity. To accommodate the inherent semantic imbalance, we explicitly bifurcate the expert pool into semantic experts and generic experts, with semantic experts capturing high-level semantic abstraction and generic experts preserving residual visual information and flexible generative capacity. Leveraging prototype-guided routing and pull-push regularization, SplitMoE enables tokens to cluster naturally by semantic attributes rather than arbitrary balancing constraints. Extensive results show that under an equivalent activated-parameter budget, SplitMoE outperforms traditional load-balanced MoEs in convergence speed, routing coherence, and video generation quality across standard benchmarks. By revealing an emergent coarse-to-fine denoising logic, SplitMoE provides the community with a modality-aware scaling path, serving as a critical reference for building large-scale video world models.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Science and Technology Beijing

ru.title: Разделённые роли экспертов: преодоление унификации в видео-генерации
ru.desc: В статье предложена архитектура SplitMoE для видео-генеративных моделей, которая преодолевает ограничения традиционных смешанных экспертов (Mixture-of-Experts). Авторы показывают, что обычные MoE попадают в ловушку унификации: независимая маршрутизация токенов и регуляризация на равномерность использования экспертов приводят к фрагментации и искажению структуры. Решение заключается в разделении пула экспертов на семантические эксперты для извлечения высокоуровневых признаков и универсальные эксперты для сохранения остаточной информации. Метод использует прототипно-ориентированную маршрутизацию и pull-push регуляризацию, что обеспечивает лучшую сходимость и качество видеогенерации при той же вычислительной бюджете.

en.title: SplitMoE: Enhancing Video Generation with Semantic Expert Clustering
en.desc: This paper introduces SplitMoE, a new architecture for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) that improves the handling of video data in generative models. Traditional MoE approaches struggle with uniform expert usage, leading to ineffective routing of tokens and poor performance on semantically complex video data. SplitMoE addresses this by dividing the expert pool into semantic and generic experts, allowing for more effective clustering of tokens based on their semantic attributes. The results demonstrate that SplitMoE significantly enhances convergence speed, routing coherence, and video generation quality compared to conventional MoE models.

zh.title: SplitMoE：打破均匀性的视觉生成新范式
zh.desc: 混合专家（MoE）是一种在视觉生成模型中扩展的有前景的范式。传统的MoE方法在同质专家池中独立地处理令牌，导致在处理视频数据时效果不佳。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了SplitMoE，它将专家池分为语义专家和通用专家，以更好地捕捉语义信息。实验结果表明，SplitMoE在收敛速度、路由一致性和视频生成质量上优于传统的负载平衡MoE。

papers.title: AutoDataBench: Can Agents Write the Data That Feeds the Self-Improvement Loop?
papers.abstract: Abstract  Recent gains in language model capability have come more from data than from architecture. Frontier labs and data companies produce verifiable agentic tasks, which supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning then turn into capability.This production line still rests on human labour and on human-in-the-loop collaboration. Automating task creation would let data production scale with compute rather than with expert headcount, would extend to more domains, and would enable a key step in recursive self-improvement (RSI). Current evaluations of an agent's ability to write such tasks measure how a model performs after training on what the agent produced. That does not match common practice in the data industry, where data is delivered sample by sample and each sample is accepted against a set of criteria rather than put straight into training. No existing evaluation asks whether an individual task meets the acceptance criteria of a data pipeline. We therefore introduce AutoDataBench. Given an original benchmark task and a record of the target model attempting it, an agent must write a new task for the same suite that meets practical acceptance standards on validity, novelty, difficulty and behavioural coverage. Across three benchmarks of executable agent tasks, no agent we evaluate scores above 20 out of 100 at the default time budget of 45 minutes. Giving the strongest agent four times as long improves its score substantially, while the cost of one usable task stays almost unchanged. Current agents can write training tasks of the required quality, but not efficiently. AutoDataBench provides a direct measure of an agent's capacity for autonomous data synthesis: one artifact at a time, judged against the criteria a production pipeline would apply, and without a training run. Code and data are available at https://github.com/StarDewXXX/AutoDataBench.

ru.title: Автоматический синтез качественных обучающих данных без участия человека
ru.desc: В статье представлена AutoDataBench - бенчмарк для оценки способности агентов самостоятельно создавать высококачественные задачи для обучения языковых моделей. Авторы показывают, что современные агенты могут генерировать задачи, соответствующие критериям валидности, новизны и сложности, но делают это неэффективно - ни один из протестированных агентов не набрал выше 20 из 100 баллов за 45 минут. Оценка проводится на уровне отдельных задач без обучающего прохода модели, что соответствует реальной практике data pipeline в индустрии. Исследование демонстрирует, что автоматизация синтеза обучающих данных необходима для масштабирования production line языковых моделей и открывает путь к рекурсивному самоулучшению систем.

en.title: Automating Task Creation for Scalable Data Production
en.desc: This paper discusses the importance of data in enhancing the capabilities of language models, emphasizing that recent advancements are more due to data quantity than architectural changes. It introduces AutoDataBench, a tool designed to automate the creation of tasks for training models, which could help scale data production without relying heavily on human experts. The evaluation method proposed assesses whether the generated tasks meet specific acceptance criteria, such as validity and novelty, rather than just their performance post-training. The findings indicate that while current agents can create tasks of acceptable quality, they do so inefficiently, highlighting the need for improved autonomous data synthesis methods.

zh.title: 自动化任务创建，提升数据生产效率
zh.desc: 最近，语言模型的能力提升主要来自于数据而非架构。前沿实验室和数据公司通过监督微调和强化学习，将可验证的任务转化为能力。这一过程仍然依赖于人类劳动和人机协作。我们提出了AutoDataBench，旨在自动化任务创建，以便数据生产能够与计算能力扩展，而不是依赖专家人数。

papers.title: Beyond Selection: Token Parameterization for Extreme Visual Token Compression
papers.abstract: Abstract  Visual-token compression is effective for improving the efficiency of vision-language models, but under extreme compression budgets, token pruning can break visual grounding while learned resamplers increase parameter count, attention cost, and training complexity. We revisit compression through a token parameterization lens, separating (i) basis transformation and structured truncation (retained subspace/compressibility) from (ii) coordinate organization (optimization and cross-modal alignment). This view yields two coupled objectives, compressibility and learnability, which we formalize as unified functionals. Guided by these objectives, we design Braco, a lightweight four-step coder that combines transform-basis truncation, input-independent basis-coordinate embeddings, budget-dependent orthogonal re-parameterization, and learned spatial residual tokens from lightweight pooling. Experiments show that Braco forms the favorable empirical accuracy-efficiency frontier under 23times--64times compression and remains competitive at 144times, reaching 95.2% accuracy while reducing prefill FLOPs by 84.2%--86.7% relative to the uncompressed upper bound. Against prior methods, Braco matches or improves accuracy while achieving up to approximately 36% end-to-end speedup and using 16.6times/78.8times lower compressor latency/FLOPs.

ru.title: Брако: эффективное сжатие визуальных токенов через переосмысление параметризации
ru.desc: В статье предложен новый подход к сжатию визуальных токенов в vision-language моделях через переосмысление параметризации токенов. Авторы разделяют задачу на две части: преобразование базиса с структурированным усечением и организацию координат для оптимизации и кросс-модальной согласованности. На основе этого анализа разработан метод Braco — лёгкий четырёхшаговый кодер, объединяющий трансформацию базиса, вложения координат и остаточные токены из облегчённого пулинга. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что Braco достигает лучшего баланса между точностью и эффективностью при сжатии в 23-64 раза, обеспечивая ускорение до 36% с минимальными вычислительными затратами.

en.title: Braco: Efficient Visual-Token Compression for Vision-Language Models
en.desc: This paper introduces Braco, a novel approach to visual-token compression for vision-language models. It separates the process into two main objectives: compressibility, which focuses on how well the model can reduce data size, and learnability, which ensures the model can still learn effectively. Braco employs a four-step coding process that optimizes both the transformation of data and the organization of coordinates, leading to significant improvements in efficiency. The results demonstrate that Braco achieves high accuracy while drastically reducing computational costs and latency compared to existing methods.

zh.title: Braco：高效的视觉-语言模型压缩方案
zh.desc: 视觉-语言模型的视觉标记压缩可以提高效率，但在极端压缩情况下，标记剪枝可能会破坏视觉基础，而学习的重采样器则增加了参数数量和训练复杂性。本文通过标记参数化的视角重新审视压缩，分离了基础变换和结构截断与坐标组织。我们提出了两个耦合目标：可压缩性和可学习性，并将其形式化为统一的函数。基于这些目标，我们设计了Braco，一个轻量级的四步编码器，能够在高压缩比下保持准确性和效率。

papers.title: Real2Gym: Building Gyms from Videos, Bringing Skills to Robots
papers.abstract: Abstract  Real-world videos provide rich demonstrations of manipulation, but turning them into reusable robot skills requires visually aligned environments, executable physical interactions, and mechanisms for learning from experience. We introduce Real2Gym, an agentic Real2Sim2Real framework that turns human and robot demonstrations into interactive simulation gyms and brings skills acquired in simulation to physical robots. The Real2Sim module reconstructs editable scenes, aligns objects and cameras with the input, validates demonstrated or retargeted actions through native physics execution, and generates task-conditioned variations with action-feasibility checks. Within these environments, the agent generates executable code for manipulation stages, observes their outcomes, and distills successful attempts and failures into reusable task procedures, object-relative motions, and recovery strategies. Through a shared perception-and-control interface, these skills guide subsequent execution in simulation and on real robots, with motions adapted to current observations and no updates to the underlying model weights. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that Real2Gym enables high-fidelity simulation environment reconstruction, outperforming GPT-6 Astra Direct Mode by 16.7% in success rate with approximately 74.9% fewer policy-execution tokens across these environments, while exceeding it by 33.3% in physical robot execution success rate across four tasks on a real Franka robot.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: От видео к роботам: автоматическое извлечение манипуляционных навыков через симуляцию
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Real2Gym — фреймворк, который превращает видео-демонстрации человека и робота в интерактивные симуляционные окружения, пригодные для обучения навыкам манипуляции. Система включает модуль Real2Sim для реконструкции редактируемых сцен с проверкой физической корректности действий, и модуль агента, который генерирует исполняемый код для манипуляционных задач, анализирует результаты и извлекает переиспользуемые процедуры и стратегии восстановления. Полученные в симуляции навыки передаются на физических роботов через общий интерфейс восприятия и управления, где движения адаптируются к текущим наблюдениям без обновления весов модели. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что Real2Gym достигает высокоточной реконструкции сцен и превосходит существующие методы на реальных робот-манипуляторах на 33.3% по успешности выполнения задач.

en.title: Transforming Real-World Videos into Robot Skills with Real2Gym
en.desc: The paper presents Real2Gym, a framework that transforms real-world video demonstrations into interactive simulation environments for robots. It includes a Real2Sim module that reconstructs scenes, aligns objects, and validates actions using physics, allowing for the generation of task-specific variations. The framework enables robots to learn from both successful and failed attempts, creating reusable skills and strategies for manipulation tasks. Real2Gym shows significant improvements in simulation and real-world execution success rates compared to existing methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in robotic skill acquisition.

zh.title: 将现实演示转化为可重用机器人技能的框架
zh.desc: 本文介绍了Real2Gym，一个将人类和机器人演示转化为交互式模拟环境的框架。该框架通过Real2Sim模块重建可编辑场景，并对输入进行对象和相机的对齐。它能够生成可执行的操作代码，并从成功和失败的尝试中提炼出可重用的任务程序和恢复策略。通过共享的感知与控制接口，这些技能可以在模拟和真实机器人上执行，且无需更新基础模型权重。

papers.title: Act First, Reason Later: Accelerating On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents via Reference-Conditioned Inverse Dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract  On-policy distillation (OPD) trains multi-turn language agents with dense teacher supervision on student-generated responses. However, standard think-then-act rollouts require lengthy reasoning before each short action, delaying environment transitions and experience collection. Generating actions directly reduces this delay but can degrade rollout quality. To address this, we propose ActFirst-OPD, an act-first, reason-later training framework that decouples environment interaction from full-response generation. The student infers and executes actions through reference-conditioned inverse dynamics using its current interaction context and a reference next observation, and switches to autonomous next-action prediction when the resulting transition deviates from the reference trajectory. From the collected interaction contexts, the student asynchronously generates full think-then-act responses for token-level teacher supervision. Experiments across 0.6B-, 1.7B-, and 4B-parameter Qwen3 students show that ActFirst-OPD achieves average wall-clock training speedups of 2.3times on ALFWorld, 1.8times on WebShop, and 4.9times on ScienceWorld over Vanilla OPD. It matches or exceeds all compared OPD baselines in mean task success rate across eight of nine benchmark-model settings. These results demonstrate that reasoning need not block acting during multi-turn agent distillation.
affiliations: College of Computing & Data Science, Nanyang Technological University
Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Brain-Inspired Intelligent Computation, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Действуй первым, размышляй потом: ускоренное дистилляционное обучение агентов
ru.desc: Статья предлагает ActFirst-OPD — новый подход к обучению многошаговых языковых агентов, который разделяет процесс взаимодействия с окружением и генерации полного ответа. Студент сначала быстро предсказывает и выполняет действия, используя обратную динамику, обусловленную контекстом взаимодействия и эталонным следующим наблюдением, а затем асинхронно генерирует полные рассуждения для обучения с учителем. Такой подход значительно ускоряет сбор опыта — в 2.3-4.9 раза быстрее стандартного метода — поскольку агент не ждёт завершения рассуждений перед каждым действием. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что предложенный метод сохраняет или превосходит качество обучения на нескольких эталонных задачах.

en.title: Act First, Reason Later: Speeding Up Multi-Turn Agent Training
en.desc: This paper introduces ActFirst-OPD, a new training framework for multi-turn language agents that improves the efficiency of on-policy distillation (OPD). Instead of waiting for complete reasoning before taking actions, ActFirst-OPD allows agents to act first and reason later, which speeds up the training process. The framework uses reference-conditioned inverse dynamics to guide the agent's actions based on its current context and a reference observation. Experimental results show that this approach significantly increases training speed while maintaining or improving task success rates compared to traditional OPD methods.

zh.title: 推理与行动并行，提升多轮代理训练效率
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的训练框架，称为ActFirst-OPD，用于多轮语言代理的在线蒸馏。该方法通过先执行动作再进行推理，减少了环境交互与完整响应生成之间的延迟。学生代理利用参考条件的逆动态推断和执行动作，并在偏离参考轨迹时切换到自主预测下一动作。实验结果表明，ActFirst-OPD在多个基准模型设置中显著提高了训练速度和任务成功率，证明了推理与行动可以并行进行。

papers.title: Org-Agent: Beyond Personal Assistants Towards Organizational Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Language model agents serving organizations must coordinate requests from multiple users while using knowledge distributed across their interactions. We identify two complementary capabilities for this setting, namely cross-user interaction and decision-making, as well as cross-user memory and knowledge use. Both capabilities are governed by organizational constraints across three aspects: user identity, authority, and access permissions; the attribution and temporal validity of information; and rules for resolving conflicting requirements across users and completion requirements for joint decisions. These constraints shape what information or decisions must be obtained before an action can proceed and what conditions must be satisfied during its execution. Motivated by this, we introduce Org-Agent, a unified constraint-centric reasoning framework that organizes task execution in three stages. Specifically, Org-Agent decomposes a task into atomic subtasks and constructs a task dependency graph whose edges encode the dependencies among them. Building on this graph, it schedules the subtasks in dependency order through topological sorting. It then executes each subtask while accounting for the task's constraints, supported by evidence-acquisition and memory-management tools. Experiments on MUSES-Bench and GroupMemBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Org-Agent on both capabilities, and ablations further support the contributions of dependency modeling and tool use.
affiliations: The Department of Computing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong SAR

ru.title: Интеллектуальная агентская система с осознанием организационных ограничений
ru.desc: В статье представлен Org-Agent — фреймворк для координации языковых моделей в организационных системах, где необходимо учитывать ограничения, связанные с идентификацией пользователей, правами доступа и конфликтующими требованиями. Подход разлагает задачи на атомарные подзадачи и строит граф зависимостей между ними, затем упорядочивает их через топологическую сортировку. При выполнении каждой подзадачи система учитывает организационные ограничения с помощью специализированных инструментов для получения доказательств и управления памятью. Экспериментальные результаты на эталонных наборах MUSES-Bench и GroupMemBench показывают эффективность подхода для обработки кросс-пользовательского взаимодействия и совместного использования знаний.

en.title: Org-Agent: Coordinating Language Model Agents for Collaborative Decision-Making
en.desc: This paper presents Org-Agent, a framework designed for language model agents to effectively manage requests from multiple users within organizations. It emphasizes two key capabilities: coordinating interactions among users and utilizing shared knowledge while adhering to organizational constraints. The framework organizes task execution into three stages, including task decomposition, dependency graph construction, and subtask scheduling, ensuring that all necessary conditions are met before actions are taken. Experimental results show that Org-Agent enhances decision-making and memory management, proving its effectiveness in complex collaborative environments.

zh.title: Org-Agent：优化多用户请求的智能决策框架
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为Org-Agent的统一约束中心推理框架，旨在帮助组织中的语言模型代理协调来自多个用户的请求。该框架具备跨用户交互与决策能力，以及跨用户记忆和知识使用能力，受到用户身份、权限和信息有效性等组织约束的影响。Org-Agent将任务分解为原子子任务，并构建任务依赖图，以便通过拓扑排序调度子任务。实验结果表明，Org-Agent在处理用户请求和满足约束条件方面表现出色。

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of Continual Learning: A Unified View of Data Attribution, Forgetting, and Plasticity Loss
papers.abstract: Abstract  Modern language models are likely to be updated throughout their lifetime rather than trained once and frozen. Each update therefore participates in a recurring cycle: decide which experience to learn from, understand what that update changes, and remain capable of learning from what comes next. We show that these challenges are governed by the same evolving update--behavior interaction. We derive a token- and layer-wise decomposition of how learning from one token changes another prediction. By separating the softmax force, shared readout geometry, and residual connections, it exposes two interaction channels and yields a forward-computable approximation. Following this interaction through time reveals a unified picture of continual adaptation. Positive interaction identifies useful experience; negative interaction produces either concentrated collision or accumulated erosion; over longer horizons, updates reshape the shared geometry mediating future learning signals, reducing their transmission. These predictions lead to effective data selection, mechanism-specific controls for interference, and a readout-based diagnostic of future learnability whose degradation predicts the benefit of restoring the readout. Across models and training regimes, the same local interaction thus explains both what an update changes now and how learning today changes what can be learned tomorrow. This view connects data attribution, forgetting, and plasticity loss as distinct regimes of the same evolving learning dynamics.

ru.title: Единая механика обновлений: как настоящее обучение определяет возможности будущего
ru.desc: Статья изучает, как языковые модели обновляются на протяжении своего жизненного цикла, анализируя взаимодействие между обновлениями и поведением модели. Авторы разработали декомпозицию на уровне токенов и слоёв, которая показывает, как обучение на одном токене влияет на предсказания других. Исследование выявляет два канала взаимодействия через разделение softmax, геометрии выходного слоя и остаточных связей, позволяя предсказать эффекты обновлений. Результаты объединяют проблемы выбора данных, катастрофического забывания и потери пластичности в единую теорию эволюционирующей динамики обучения.

en.title: Evolving Learning Dynamics in Language Models
en.desc: This paper discusses how modern language models can be continuously updated rather than being static after initial training. It introduces a framework to understand how updates affect model behavior by analyzing the interactions between tokens and layers during learning. The authors identify two main types of interactions: positive, which enhances learning from experiences, and negative, which can lead to forgetting or interference. By examining these interactions over time, the study provides insights into effective data selection and the dynamics of continual learning in language models.

zh.title: 持续学习：更新与行为的交互
zh.desc: 现代语言模型在其生命周期内可能会不断更新，而不是一次性训练后就不再改变。每次更新都涉及一个循环过程：决定学习哪些经验，理解更新带来的变化，并保持对未来学习的能力。我们展示了这些挑战由不断演变的更新与行为交互所主导。通过分解学习如何从一个token影响另一个预测，我们揭示了持续适应的统一图景，连接了数据归因、遗忘和可塑性损失等不同学习动态。

papers.title: ALICE: In-context, Zero-shot, Mutual Information Estimation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Estimating mutual information (MI) from samples is a central objective in a variety of scientific fields. Modern neural estimators are accurate in the large-data regime, but they fall short when data is scarce, and each must be fit anew for every distribution under study. Current estimators are moreover tied to specific data types. These constraints limit their adoption in many applications where per-distribution training is impractical and sample sizes are small.   We present ALICE, a foundation model that removes per-distribution training, while achieving competitive estimation accuracy. Trained exclusively on a broad family of synthetic distributions, ALICE acts as an in-context estimator of rectified-flow velocity fields: conditioned on samples of an unseen distribution, it estimates that distribution's velocity field without any explicit training. MI is then obtained through a fixed identity that integrates the squared difference between the joint and conditional fields. We validate ALICE on a standard, challenging benchmark and apply it in three domains, biology, genetics, and neuroscience, whose data the model has never seen. For the first time, we show that a single model closes the gap with neural estimators trained separately for each distribution, while natively supporting different data dimensionality and sample cardinality, enabling zero-shot MI analysis across scientific domains.

ru.title: Foundation Model для универсальной оценки взаимной информации без переобучения
ru.desc: В статье представлена ALICE — foundation model для оценки взаимной информации (MI) из выборок данных, которая обучается на синтетических распределениях и может работать с новыми, ранее не встречавшимися распределениями без дополнительного обучения. Модель использует in-context learning для оценки полей скоростей (velocity fields) через rectified flow и вычисляет взаимную информацию с помощью фиксированной формулы, интегрирующей разницу между совместным и условным полями. ALICE впервые достигает конкурентной точности с нейросетевыми оценщиками, специально обученными для каждого распределения, но при этом работает в zero-shot режиме и поддерживает данные разной размерности и объёма. Модель успешно валидирована на стандартных бенчмарках и протестирована на реальных данных из биологии, генетики и нейронауки, демонстрируя применимость across different scientific domains.

en.title: ALICE: Zero-Shot Mutual Information Estimation Across Domains
en.desc: This paper introduces ALICE, a novel model designed to estimate mutual information (MI) without the need for training on specific distributions. Unlike traditional neural estimators that require large datasets and individual training for each distribution, ALICE leverages a foundation model trained on a variety of synthetic distributions. It can estimate the velocity fields of unseen distributions by conditioning on sample data, achieving competitive accuracy in MI estimation. The model demonstrates versatility across different scientific fields, including biology, genetics, and neuroscience, enabling zero-shot analysis of MI with minimal data requirements.

zh.title: ALICE：无须单独训练的互信息估计器
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为ALICE的模型，用于估计互信息（MI），特别是在数据稀缺的情况下。ALICE通过在广泛的合成分布上进行训练，消除了对每个分布单独训练的需求，能够在未见过的数据上进行估计。该模型在生物学、遗传学和神经科学等领域的应用中表现出色，首次实现了在不同数据维度和样本数量下的零-shot MI 分析。ALICE的准确性与传统的神经估计器相当，展示了其在科学研究中的广泛适用性。

papers.title: PMOPD: Task Ordering, Cycling, and Parameter-Update Subspace Protection in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Abstract  Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) has emerged as a popular post-training paradigm for integrating specialized capabilities in frontier language models. Existing OPD research has primarily focused on optimizing single-task distillation through objective design, distillation scope, and teacher signal construction, whereas MOPD must aggregate multiple capabilities in shared parameters and address the resulting capability seesaw, in which improving one domain suppresses capabilities acquired from another. Inspired by the distinctive update geometry of OPD, we find that parameter updates from different tasks rapidly concentrate in their respective low-dimensional subspaces during MOPD, providing a direct geometric basis for identifying and controlling cross-task interference. We therefore propose PMOPD (Projection-based Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation), which constructs subspace memories from the cumulative parameter displacements of different tasks and projects both gradients and optimizer updates to remove components that interfere with protected task directions. We further develop a lightweight conflict probe to characterize task interactions and guide task ordering, together with a cycling strategy that balances subspace estimation and timely task revisitation. Experiments on representative Code, Reason, and Math tasks show that PMOPD improves every evaluated capability over MOPD, raising the average score across the three tasks by 2.54 points on Qwen2.5-7B and 2.09 points on Llama-3.1-8B. These consistent gains establish geometry-aware optimization as an effective and transferable approach to balanced multi-teacher distillation.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Геометрическое равновесие: контроль конфликтов в многоучительском дистилляционном обучении
ru.desc: В статье предложен метод PMOPD для обучения больших языковых моделей сразу у нескольких учителей, решающий проблему взаимного подавления способностей (когда улучшение в одной задаче ухудшает качество в другой). Авторы обнаружили, что обновления параметров разных задач концентрируются в отдельных низкоразмерных подпространствах, и используют это геометрическое свойство для предотвращения конфликтов между задачами. Метод проецирует градиенты и обновления оптимизатора, удаляя компоненты, мешающие обучению важных направлений, а также включает механизм для определения порядка обучения задач. Экспериментальные результаты на задачах кодирования, логических рассуждений и математики показывают улучшение на несколько пунктов по сравнению с базовым методом многоучительского обучения.

en.title: Balancing Skills in Language Models with Geometry-Aware Distillation
en.desc: This paper introduces PMOPD, a method for improving multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) in language models. MOPD aims to combine various specialized skills while managing the challenge of capability seesaw, where enhancing one skill can weaken another. The authors leverage the geometric properties of parameter updates to minimize interference between tasks by projecting updates into low-dimensional subspaces. Experimental results demonstrate that PMOPD significantly enhances performance across multiple tasks, showcasing the effectiveness of geometry-aware optimization in multi-teacher settings.

zh.title: 几何感知优化：提升多教师蒸馏的有效方法
zh.desc: 多教师在线蒸馏（MOPD）是一种新兴的后训练方法，用于整合前沿语言模型中的专业能力。现有的在线蒸馏研究主要集中在单任务蒸馏的优化上，而MOPD需要在共享参数中聚合多种能力，并解决能力之间的相互抑制问题。我们提出了一种基于投影的多教师在线蒸馏（PMOPD），通过构建子空间记忆来识别和控制跨任务干扰。实验结果表明，PMOPD在多个任务上均显著提升了能力表现，验证了几何感知优化在平衡多教师蒸馏中的有效性。

papers.title: Improved Distributional Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Distributional Diffusion Models (DDMs) replace the standard mean-prediction denoiser with a distributional denoiser trained via a scoring rule objective, learning a stochastic approximation to p(x_1 mid x_t) rather than its conditional mean. However, scaling DDMs to modern image-generation settings faces two obstacles: (i) multi-particle training incurs overhead that scales with the number of particles, (ii) DDMs use globally fixed scoring rule hyperparameters, forcing a single trade-off across sampling budgets. We mitigate these limitations by deferring particle expansion to late transformer layers, and the hyperparameter trade-off by introducing time-dependent scoring rule schedules informed by the dynamical regimes of~Biroli2024. Combined with a DiT-based latent setup, these changes make DDM training practical on class-conditional ImageNet-256^2, achieving 4.48 FID at 4 steps and 2.38 at 50 steps with DiT-XL/2, from a single model trained from scratch in one stage, without a teacher, self-distillation or JVPs. The result is a stochastic few-step generator whose FID does not degrade as the sampling budget grows from 4 to 50 NFE, and the same recipe transfers to text-to-image generation. Code and pre-trained models available at https://github.com/CompVis/iDDM.

ru.title: Практичные распределительные модели диффузии для быстрой генерации изображений
ru.desc: В работе предложены Distributional Diffusion Models (DDM) — модели диффузии, которые обучаются предсказывать полное распределение p(x_1|x_t) вместо его условного среднего, используя объективную функцию на основе scoring rule. Авторы решили две ключевые проблемы масштабирования: снизили вычислительные издержки многочастичного обучения, отложив расширение частиц на поздние слои трансформера, и справились с жесткими гиперпараметрами, введя динамические расписания scoring rule. Модель на основе DiT достигает высокого качества генерации на ImageNet-256 (FID 4.48 при 4 шагах и 2.38 при 50 шагах) без использования учителя или самодистилляции. Полученный стохастический генератор эффективно работает как при малом, так и при большом количестве шагов сэмплирования.

en.title: Revolutionizing Image Generation with Distributional Diffusion Models
en.desc: This paper introduces Distributional Diffusion Models (DDMs), which enhance image generation by using a distributional denoiser instead of a mean-prediction denoiser. The authors address two main challenges in scaling DDMs: the overhead from multi-particle training and the limitations of fixed scoring rule hyperparameters. They propose solutions by delaying particle expansion to later transformer layers and implementing time-dependent scoring rule schedules. These innovations allow for effective training on ImageNet-256^2, resulting in a high-quality stochastic generator that maintains performance across varying sampling budgets.

zh.title: 分布扩散模型：高效的图像生成新方法
zh.desc: 分布扩散模型（DDMs）通过评分规则目标训练分布去噪器，替代了标准的均值预测去噪器，从而学习条件概率的随机近似。该模型在现代图像生成中面临两个主要挑战：多粒子训练的开销随粒子数量增加而增加，以及使用全局固定的评分规则超参数，限制了采样预算的灵活性。为了解决这些问题，本文将粒子扩展推迟到变换器的后期层，并引入时间依赖的评分规则调度，以适应动态状态。通过这些改进，DDM在ImageNet-256^2上的训练变得可行，生成的图像质量在不同采样预算下保持稳定。

papers.title: Scaffolding Minds: Optimizing Latent Visual Target Representations for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract  Latent reasoning has advanced multimodal reasoning through a two-stage training paradigm: (1) a helper image is encoded into latent tokens to teach visual chain-of-thought during a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage, and (2) these latent tokens are further refined with reward feedback during a reinforcement learning (RL) stage. In this paper, we identify two key limitations of this framework, one in each stage. First, the SFT stage typically relies on an off-the-shelf vision encoder to encode the helper image, yielding suboptimal latent representations that may not be well aligned with the downstream reasoning task. Second, existing RL methods treat the latent component only through deterministic regularization, which constrains policy drift but does not create alternative latent trajectories for exploration. To address these limitations, we propose Scaffolding Minds. Our approach learns a dedicated scaffolding encoder that provides an optimized target in latent space, and learns both the mean and variance of the RL sampler. We further show that these two improvements are complementary, together yielding substantial gains over strong baselines. Empirically, our method improves over the strongest latent reasoning baseline by +9.5 points on FrozenLake spatial planning, with the gain widening to +19 points on the 32x32 grids, and by +5.6 points on average across nine visual-centric reasoning benchmarks.

ru.title: Оптимизация латентного пространства для улучшения визуального рассуждения моделей
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается улучшение мультимодального рассуждения через латентные представления, которые обучаются в два этапа: сначала с помощью supervised fine-tuning с вспомогательными изображениями, а затем через reinforcement learning с сигналами обратной связи. Авторы выявили два ключевых ограничения этого подхода: неоптимальные латентные представления от стандартных vision encoder'ов и недостаточное исследование пространства латентных траекторий при обучении с подкреплением. Предложенный метод Scaffolding Minds использует специальный encoder для получения оптимизированных целевых представлений и обучает как среднее значение, так и дисперсию политики RL, что позволяет лучше исследовать альтернативные траектории. Эмпирические результаты показывают значительные улучшения: +9.5 балла на FrozenLake, +19 баллов на более крупных сетках и +5.6 балла в среднем на девяти бенчмарках визуального рассуждения.

en.title: Enhancing Latent Reasoning with Scaffolding Minds
en.desc: This paper introduces Scaffolding Minds, a novel approach to enhance latent reasoning in multimodal tasks. It addresses two main issues in the existing two-stage training paradigm: the use of suboptimal vision encoders during supervised fine-tuning and the limitations of deterministic regularization in reinforcement learning. By implementing a dedicated scaffolding encoder, the method optimizes latent representations and allows for better exploration of latent trajectories. The results demonstrate significant performance improvements on various reasoning benchmarks, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed enhancements.

zh.title: 优化潜在推理，提升多模态推理能力
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种新的方法，称为Scaffolding Minds，旨在改进多模态推理中的潜在推理框架。该方法通过引入专门的支架编码器，优化潜在空间中的目标表示，从而解决了传统方法在监督微调阶段的不足。其次，我们的方法还学习了强化学习采样器的均值和方差，促进了潜在轨迹的探索。实验结果表明，该方法在多个视觉推理基准上显著提高了性能，尤其是在FrozenLake空间规划任务中取得了9.5分的提升。

papers.title: StructRL: Online Structured Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Tasks
papers.abstract: Abstract  Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform well on shorter-horizon manipulation tasks but still struggle with long-horizon tasks that require multiple dependent manipulations from a single command. Online reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies through environment interaction, yet many existing methods provide reward only after the complete task succeeds. However, such terminal supervision is sparse and does not distinguish early failures from rollouts that make substantial partial progress. We propose StructRL, an online RL framework that constructs structured intermediate supervision from verifiable subtask completions. StructRL decomposes each task into verifiable subtasks, grants intermediate rewards only after the prerequisite subtasks have been completed, and scales each reward according to completion pace. Across RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Long with GR00T-N1.5 and pi 0.5, StructRL consistently outperforms evaluated online RL baselines. These results show that verifiable, structured intermediate rewards improve long-horizon VLA post-training. Code is available at https://github.com/amazon-science/StructRL.

ru.title: Структурированное подкрепление для долгосрочных манипуляций роботами
ru.desc: В статье предлагается StructRL — фреймворк онлайн-обучения с подкреплением для улучшения vision-language-action моделей на задачах долгосрочного манипулирования. Авторы решают проблему разреженной награды, разлагая задачи на проверяемые подзадачи и предоставляя промежуточные награды только после их завершения. Система масштабирует величину награды в зависимости от темпа выполнения, что позволяет отличить ранние ошибки от частичного прогресса. Экспериментальные результаты на наборах данных RoboCasa365 и LIBERO-Long показывают, что структурированное промежуточное подкрепление значительно улучшает post-training больших мультимодальных моделей для робототехники.

en.title: Empowering Long-Horizon Tasks with Structured Rewards
en.desc: This paper introduces StructRL, a novel online reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance vision-language-action (VLA) models for long-horizon manipulation tasks. Unlike traditional methods that provide rewards only upon complete task success, StructRL offers structured intermediate rewards based on the completion of verifiable subtasks. This approach allows for better learning by recognizing partial progress and adjusting rewards according to the pace of subtask completion. The results demonstrate that StructRL significantly improves the performance of VLA models in complex environments compared to existing online RL methods.

zh.title: 结构化中间奖励提升长时间任务表现
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为StructRL的在线强化学习框架，旨在改善视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在长时间任务中的表现。该框架通过将任务分解为可验证的子任务，并在完成前置子任务后给予中间奖励，从而提供结构化的中间监督。与传统方法相比，StructRL能够更好地区分早期失败和部分进展，提升了长时间任务的学习效率。实验结果表明，StructRL在RoboCasa365和LIBERO-Long数据集上均优于现有的在线强化学习基线。

papers.title: Understanding On-Policy Distillation: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective via Sparse Crosscoders
papers.abstract: Abstract  On-policy distillation (OPD) is a widely adopted post-training technique for LLM reasoning. It is commonly believed to transfer knowledge from a stronger teacher, yet what OPD actually distills into the student's internal representations remains unclear. We study this question with sparse crosscoders, which learn one feature dictionary shared by the student before and after OPD and the teacher. Standard crosscoder analyses, however, identify model-specific features but cannot tell how a model's use of its features changes, since all models are encoded into one set of feature activations. We therefore propose the swap readout, which reads each student checkpoint's feature activations on its own, measuring how training changes the student's use of each feature, even for checkpoints unseen by the crosscoder. Across three OPD settings, we find that OPD neither creates features nor passes on the teacher's own, and leaves the firing rates of over 98% of the student's frequently used features within 20%. We further examine the SFT warm-up on the teacher's rollouts that commonly precedes OPD and makes it more effective. Rather than adding features, the warm-up reweights the shared ones in two ways. First, it already raises and lowers many of the features that OPD later raises and lowers, doing part of OPD's work in advance. Second, it changes features that OPD alone would not, notably those for conversation format, reasoning style, and mathematical notation, and these changes persist through OPD. Imposing this reweighting on a directly distilled student's features, without changing its weights, brings its accuracy close to that of the warmed-up student, whereas the same change on shuffled features does not. Together, these findings suggest that OPD reweights existing features rather than acquiring new ones: the student learns from the teacher how to use the features they already share.
